title: Hylton Planetarium — Service Modernization
goal: Increase program reach and operational clarity for educators, parents, and patrons.
summary: Service design + brand refresh + booking-friendly IA for a county planetarium serving educators and the public.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
Role: UX & Digital Strategy (engagement lead)
Domain: Education, Public Services
Scope: Service design, brand refresh, web experience, booking flow
Team: [X designers, Y engineers, Z content/photography]
Timeframe: [Q#/Year – Q#/Year]

sections.title: Goal & Constraints
sections.body: Unify how educators and patrons discover programs, understand availability, and book—within school policies, seasonal demand spikes, and limited staff capacity.

sections.title: What I Led
sections.body:
• Org & Ops — Pricing, budget, proposal; team hiring; timeline; governance; approval checkpoints.
• Research & Insights — Educator/patron interviews; heuristics review; content audit; peer venue scan.
• Product & IA — Service model; task-first IA (Programs, Booking, Educator Resources, Community Events).
• Design & Systems — Brand refresh; photography direction/editing; component library; mobile/desktop booking; content writing.
• Delivery & Quality — Accessibility/508; heuristics QA; release readiness; final sign-off.
• Stakeholders & Decisions — Educator/staff workshops; decision reviews; monthly metric check-ins.

sections.title: Research & Discovery
sections.body: We spoke with educators and front-office staff, reviewed the current experience with a heuristics checklist, inventoried content and schedules, and scanned comparable venues to calibrate expectations for booking and field-trip planning.

artifacts.caption: Key questions and decision criteria
artifacts.alt: One-page interview guide with educator questions

artifacts.caption: Top five issues prioritized by impact on booking completion

sections.title: Mental Models → IA
sections.body: We grouped tasks by audience intent (find a show, book, plan a field trip, teacher resources) and validated labels with a lightweight card sort. These inputs defined a four-pillar IA: Programs, Booking, Educator Resources, Community Events.

artifacts.caption: Programs, Booking, Educator Resources, Community Events

sections.title: Information Architecture
sections.body: Program pages follow a consistent “What / When / How to Attend” template. Calendars consolidate capacity hints and seasonal events. The IA trims dead-end pages and reduces pogo-sticking for availability.

artifacts.caption: Task cues for booking
artifacts.alt: Program template with clear CTA and details

sections.title: Prototypes (Lo-Fi → Hi-Fi)
sections.body: We validated low-fidelity flows for discovery → booking → confirmation, then delivered high-fidelity screens for mobile and desktop with clear microcopy and a11y cues.

sections.title: Operating Mechanisms
sections.body: We installed a11y/quality gates, a content style guide, and a monthly measurement loop to track booking completion, email volume, and page findability; results informed quick follow-ups rather than rework sprints.

sections.title: Outcomes
sections.body:
Discoverability improved, booking decisions happened faster, support emails declined, and the brand presented consistently across print and digital.
